description: Verify a Forestrie receipt against the EXACT registered payload bytes and an entry id, at a trust root you choose. Mirrors `forestrie verify`. Offline: no network, no key, no account. Returns both the mechanical stages and the four trust questions. KS256 contract roots take an optional ks256Attestation (fetched elsewhere; this tool never calls the chain; several go in ks256Attestations).

path.description: filesystem path, read by the stdio adapter

ks256Attestation.description: ERC-1271 attestation artifact (encodeKs256Attestation CBOR) for a KS256 CONTRACT root. Fetched elsewhere — this server never touches the network: use mcp-resolve's `fetch_ks256_attestation` tool or forestrie-cli's `fetch-ks256-attestation`. With it a contract-rooted delegation verifies as valid under the contract's signers at the attested block. Usable with the genesis, known-log-key and checkpoint-chain roots (checkpoint-chain also needs trust.genesis for the forest chain id; one attestation binds one certificate, so a chain whose links were signed under several certificates needs one attestation per certificate: give them in ks256Attestations). Not with known-accumulator. Trust: the attestation is unsigned and only as good as whoever fetched it; accept one only from a party you would trust to read the chain for you — {b64: <standard base64>} (base64 is accepted as an alias), or {path: <a file the local server reads>}

ks256Attestations.description: Several ERC-1271 attestations (each encodeKs256Attestation CBOR, {b64: <standard base64>} (base64 is accepted as an alias), or {path: <a file the local server reads>}) for a KS256 CONTRACT root that signed more than one delegation certificate (a Safe that rotated its delegate). Each certificate takes the attestation whose digest and signature hash are its own. Combined with ks256Attestation when both are given. Every attestation is reported in the result as used or unused with a reason (ks256Attestations): none is silently ignored. Same roots and trust caveats as ks256Attestation.

oneOf.description: Trust a log owner key you obtained out of band: a 64-byte P-256 key (keyXy) or a 20-byte KS256 address (ks256Address). Same questions as genesis; the key-to-log binding is ASSERTED by you, not proven — an address in particular proves nothing about which log it owns. A contract (Safe) address needs ks256Attestation on the tool call to verify offline.

oneOf.description: Fold a retained checkpoint chain and match any authenticated link. Answers split-view. Needs genesis or keyXy to root the first link. Each link's delegation certificate limits are enforced: a link signed beyond the certificate's mmrEnd, or below its mmrStart, fails delegation_out_of_range, and a link covering the receipt's leaf signed under a certificate that had expired when the leaf was sequenced fails delegation_expired (never wall-clock). A KS256 contract (Safe) genesis root takes ks256Attestation on the tool call (one per delegation certificate: several in ks256Attestations). Failures carry the typed reason, with stage/detail/failedLink naming the link.

ks256Attestation.description: present only when a supplied ERC-1271 attestation was needed for the run to pass (the first one, when several were): a contract root is valid under its signers at THIS block only

ks256Attestations.description: every supplied attestation, accounted for: used ones carried the run (valid under the contract's signers at each named block only); unused ones say why (not_needed, no_matching_certificate, duplicate); rejected ones were tried for a link's certificate and refused. Index is the position in the supplied list (ks256Attestation first, then ks256Attestations)
